daily_brief: The human cost of Russia's war in Ukraine came into stark focus today as leaked Russian government statistics analyzed by the BBC revealed nearly 500,000 Russian soldiers have died since 2022 [BBC], a figure the Kremlin declined to confirm, stating only the defence ministry can disclose casualties [France 24]. Meanwhile, Ukraine continued long-range strikes, claiming damage to five Russian military jets at an airfield 300km east of Moscow [BBC], while defending its weekend naval drone attacks on Russian vessels in Libya that killed two Libyan soldiers [RFI, Guardian]. On the economic front, the Trump administration announced sweeping new tariffs targeting 14 major trading partners including the EU, China, and India, based on a probe into excess industrial capacity [The Hindu, ABC Australia]. India faces a 25% tariff, second only to Vietnam's 35% [The Hindu]. In response to technological competition, the EU unveiled plans for a €50 billion fund to accelerate AI and quantum computing development, aiming to lead the world in quantum technology by 2030 [RFI, Le Monde]. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, reinstated after resigning over affairs including one with an alleged Chinese spy, apologized to staff and revealed he is in daily therapy [RNZ], while US Attorney General Todd Blanche deflected questions about federal investigations into the company [BBC].

top_stories.headline: Leaked Russian Data Reveals Nearly 500,000 Soldiers Dead in Ukraine War
bullets: BBC analysis of 11 million leaked Rosstat death records shows at least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the 2022 invasion began
Data was obtained by Belarusian hacker group Cyber Partisans and Ukraine's Silent Crow; BBC Russian matched 90% of records with its own confirmed death list
Russia's statistics agency admitted to a cyber-attack but denied protected information was leaked; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said only the defence ministry can officially report casualties
Military experts estimate true death toll could range between 530,000 and 700,000 when accounting for incomplete reporting

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Led investigation, presented detailed methodology and data verification

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Focused on Kremlin's refusal to comment and cited range up to 700,000

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Reported same figures in context of Libya strikes story

top_stories.headline: Trump Administration Announces Sweeping New Tariffs on 14 Major Trading Partners
bullets: New tariffs target China, EU, India, Japan, South Korea, Vietnam, and eight other economies based on probe into excess industrial capacity
India faces 25% tariff (second-highest after Vietnam's 35%); tariffs for other partners range from 10-20%; Australia not affected
Tariffs stack on top of previous duties already imposed during Trump's second term; some Chinese goods face combined rate of 45%
Move comes despite midterm election setback and Reuters/Ipsos poll showing 62% of Americans support repealing tariffs

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Focused on India-specific impact, noted potential reduction to 17% if trade agreement reached

sources.name: ABC Australia
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Australia's exemption and legal context of SCOTUS ruling

top_stories.headline: EU Unveils €50 Billion Fund for AI and Quantum Computing to Compete with US and China
bullets: European Commission announced Sovereign Tech Equity Fund targeting €50 billion to boost AI and quantum computing capabilities
EU aims to lead the world in quantum technology by 2030 and avoid losing further ground to competitors
New rules will favor EU companies for public contracts in critical technology sectors
EU technology chief Henna Virkkunen cited cybersecurity risks from quantum computing, including ability to break encryption protecting digital data

sources.framing_note: Detailed technical benefits including medical applications and military communications

sources.name: Le Monde

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Defends Lethal Drone Strikes on Russian Ships in Libya as Two Libyan Soldiers Die
bullets: Ukraine confirmed using seven naval drones launched from a mothership to attack Russian vessels in Benghazi, sinking corvette Merkury
Two Libyan army personnel died from wounds sustained in Sunday's attack; Libya's eastern government threatens retaliation
France's Foreign Minister defended strikes as Ukraine exercising 'absolute right to self-defence'; Italy raised concerns with Kyiv
Operation conducted 1,500 miles from Ukraine's frontline marks significant geographic expansion of the conflict

sources.framing_note: Led with French FM's defense of Ukraine's actions

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Detailed operational aspects and confirmed Ukraine's acknowledgment

sources.name: ABC Australia
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Libya's retaliation threats and escalation concerns

top_stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Apologizes to Staff, Reveals Daily Therapy After Reinstatement
bullets: Huang apologized during all-staff meeting for violating company code of conduct, said he 'made some terrible mistakes'
CEO revealed he is now in therapy for 90 minutes daily; thanked his wife and children and said he was grateful for second chance
Huang dismissed suggestions that Trump orchestrated his return, saying board made decision independently
US Attorney General Todd Blanche deflected questions about federal investigations, backed Nvidia as 'good corporate citizen'
